question: Ciliary movement is found in
hint: Hint for Types of Movement: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Types of Movement.

solution: Correct option is (3). Ciliated epithelium lines the trachea (moves mucus and dust) and the fallopian tube (moves the ovum). Monocytes and macrophages show amoeboid movement.

question: Which of the following includes non-muscular movement? Protoplasmic streaming Pseudopodial movements Flagellar movements Ciliary movement
hint: Hint for Types of Movement: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Types of Movement.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Types of Movement
solution: Correct option is (3). Cytoplasmic streaming, pseudopodial (amoeboid), flagellar and ciliary movements all occur without muscle tissue.

question: Which of the following is not an example of flagellar movement?
options: Maintenance of water current in the canal system of sponges
Movement of ova in fallopian tube
hint: Hint for Types of Movement: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Types of Movement.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Types of Movement
solution: Correct option is (3). Movement of ova in the fallopian tube is by cilia.

question: Passage of ova through female reproductive tract is facilitated mainly by
hint: Hint for Types of Movement: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Types of Movement.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Types of Movement
solution: Correct option is (2). Ciliated epithelium of the fallopian tube moves the ovum.

question: Which of the following cells in our body exhibit amoeboid movement?
hint: Hint for Types of Movement: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Types of Movement.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Types of Movement
solution: Correct option is (3). Macrophages and leucocytes move by pseudopodia (amoeboid movement)

question: Read the following statements. I. Locomotion is a voluntary movement that changes the place or location of the organism. II. All movements are locomotions. III. In Paramecium, cilia help in the movement of food as well as in locomotion. Choose the correct option.
hint: Hint for Types of Movement: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Types of Movement.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Types of Movement
solution: Correct option is (2). I is true: voluntary movements that change place are called locomotion. II is false: all locomotions are movements but all movements are not locomotions (e.g. ciliary beating in the trachea, streaming of protoplasm). III is true: in Paramoecium the cilia move food through the cytopharynx and also help in locomotion. So only I and III are correct.

question: Consider the following statements. I. Macrophages exhibit amoeboid movement using pseudopodia. II. Microfilaments (cytoskeletal elements) are also involved in amoeboid movement. III. Ciliary movement helps in the passage of ova through the female reproductive tract. IV. Leucocytes move by means of cilia. How many of the above statements are correct?
hint: Hint for Types of Movement: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Types of Movement.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Types of Movement
solution: Correct option is (3). I, II and III are true. IV is false: leucocytes (like macrophages) show amoeboid movement effected by pseudopodia formed by streaming of protoplasm, not ciliary movement. Hence three statements are correct.

question: Read the following statements. I. Cilia and flagella are outgrowths of the nuclear membrane. II. Flagellar movement helps in the swimming of spermatozoa and maintenance of water current in the canal system of sponges. III. Cilia help in the movement of food through the cytopharynx in Paramecium. Choose the correct option.
hint: Hint for Types of Movement: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Types of Movement.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Types of Movement
solution: Correct option is (2). II and III are correct. I is incorrect: cilia and flagella are outgrowths of the cell (plasma) membrane.

question: Assertion (A): All locomotions are movements but all movements are not locomotions. Reason (R): Locomotion is generally for search of food, shelter, mate, suitable breeding grounds favourable climatic conditions or to escape from enemies or predators.
options: If both Assertion & Reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both Assertion & Reason are true but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If Assertion is true statement but Reason is false
If both Assertion and Reason are false statements
hint: Hint for Types of Movement: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Types of Movement.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Types of Movement
solution: Correct option is (2). Both true; R gives the purpose of locomotion, not the reason for A.

question: Assertion (A): Amoeba shows simple form of movement. Reason (R): Streaming of protoplasm is found in amoeba.
options: If both assertion and reason is true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason is true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason is false.
hint: Hint for Types of Movement: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Types of Movement.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Types of Movement
solution: Correct option is (a). Both assertion and reason are true. Amoeba moves by pseudopodia formed through streaming of protoplasm, which is a simple form of movement, so the reason correctly explains the assertion.

question: Assertion (A): Tentacles in hydra perform multiple functions. Reason (R): Tentacles in hydra are used for capturing it’s prey and as well as for locomotion.
options: If both assertion and reason is true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason is true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason is false.
hint: Hint for Types of Movement: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Types of Movement.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Types of Movement
solution: Correct option is (a). Both are true. Hydra uses its tentacles for capturing prey and also for locomotion, i.e. they perform multiple functions, so the reason explains the assertion.

question: Assertion (A): Macrophages and leucocytes in blood exhibit amoeboid movement. Reason (R): They can form pseudopodia by streaming of protoplasm.
options: If both assertion and reason is true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason is true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason is false.
hint: Hint for Types of Movement: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Types of Movement.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Types of Movement
solution: Correct option is (a). Both are true. Amoeboid movement is effected by pseudopodia formed by the streaming of protoplasm, as in Amoeba, so the reason explains the assertion.

question: Assertion (A): We can remove dust particles and some foreign substances inhaled along with the atmospheric air from trachea. Reason (R): Trachea is lined with ciliated epithelium.
options: If both assertion and reason is true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason is true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason is false.
hint: Hint for Types of Movement: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Types of Movement.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Types of Movement
solution: Correct option is (a). Both are true. The coordinated movement of the cilia of the ciliated epithelium lining the trachea removes dust particles and foreign substances, so the reason explains the assertion.

question: How many of the following features is/are correct about red muscle fibres? (i) Myoglobin content is high. (ii) Rich in mitochondria. (iii) Amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum is high. (iv) Carry out aerobic oxidation for ATP production. (v) They are thinner than white muscle fibres.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). Red fibres have abundant myoglobin, many mitochondria, work by aerobic oxidation and are thinner, so (i), (ii), (iv) and (v) are correct. (iii) is incorrect because red fibres have less sarcoplasmic reticulum than white fibres. Hence four statements are correct.

question: Choose the incorrect statement
options: A-band has both actin and myosin filaments
Length of actin and myosin is not affected during contraction
Length of A-band decreases during contraction of muscle
In a myofibril each thick filament is surrounded by six thin filaments
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). During contraction thin filaments slide over thick filaments. The A-band (length of thick filaments) stays constant, while the I-band and H-zone shorten.

question: Read the following statements about the mechanism of muscle contraction. (A) Acetylcholine is released when the neural signal reaches the motor end plate. (B) Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by CNS via sensory neuron. (C) During muscle contraction isotropic band get elongated. (D) Repeated activation of the muscle can lead to lactic acid accumulation. Choose the option stating correct statements.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). A and D are true. B is false (the signal travels via a motor neuron). C is false (the isotropic I-band shortens during contraction).

question: During muscle contraction length of
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). The A-band (thick filaments) keeps constant length; the I-band and H-zone decrease.

question: The H-zone in the skeletal muscle fibre is due to
options: The central gap between myosin filaments in the A-band
Central gap between actin filaments extending through myosin filaments in the A-band
Extension of myosin filaments in the central portion of the A-band
The absence of myofibrils in the central portion of A-band
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). The H-zone is the central region of the A-band where thin (actin) filaments do not reach, leaving only thick filaments.

question: The type of muscles present in our
options: Tongue are smooth muscle fibres and fusiform in shape
Heart are involuntary and unstriated smooth muscles
Lower third part of oesophagus are striated and involuntary
Lower legs are striated and voluntary
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). Muscles of the limbs are skeletal (striated, voluntary). The tongue is skeletal, the heart is striated and involuntary, and the lower oesophagus is smooth.

question: Which is not true for red muscle fibres?
options: Muscles contain a red coloured oxygen storing pigment
They can be exemplified by flight muscles of kites
These muscles are also called aerobic muscles
They have faster rate of contraction than white muscle fibres
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). Red fibres (myoglobin-rich, aerobic) contract slowly; white fibres contract faster.

question: The phosphogen that helps the regeneration of ATP from ADP during muscle contraction in vertebrates is
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). Creatine phosphate donates its phosphate to ADP to regenerate ATP in vertebrate muscle.

question: Muscle fatigue is the result of ________ in/of skeletal muscle. Choose the option that fills the blank correctly.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). Repeated contraction causes lactic acid accumulation (anaerobic breakdown) and depletion of ATP/creatine phosphate, producing fatigue.

question: When muscle is at rest but a certain amount of contraction still maintains, this is called
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). A small continuous partial contraction of muscle at rest is muscle tone.

question: Troponin
options: Covers the active site for actin
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). The TnC subunit of troponin binds Ca2+, which moves tropomyosin away from the active sites on actin. (Tropomyosin covers the active sites; the myosin head is globular.)

question: Mark the true statement.
options: Biceps are extensor muscles of the arm.
Tetanus refers to sustained contraction of muscle.
Muscles make up about 80 percent of body weight in an adult human.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). Tetanus is sustained contraction. Biceps are flexors, muscles are mesodermal in origin, and muscles form about 40-50% of body weight.

question: Choose the option which includes correct events occurring during muscle contraction. (A) Size of A band remains the same (B) Size of H zone becomes smaller (C) Size of I band decreases
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). During contraction the A-band stays the same, while the H-zone and I-band become smaller. All three statements are correct.

question: Cardiac muscle fibres are different from those of skeletal muscle fibres as the former are
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). Both are striated, but cardiac muscle is involuntary while skeletal muscle is voluntary.

question: During the muscle contraction, which of the following does not occur?
options: No change in length of actin filaments
Sliding movement of myosin over actin
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). In the sliding filament model the thin (actin) filaments slide over the thick filaments toward the centre of the sarcomere; the A-band and filament lengths do not change, the sarcomere shortens. Option (3) is the one stated as not occurring.

question: Match column A with column B and select the correct option. Column A Column B a. Sarcomere I. Ectodermal b. Rigor mortis II. Cardiac muscles c. Iris muscles III. Extreme rigidity of muscles in dead individual d. Intercalated discs IV. Contractile unit of skeletal muscle fibres
options: a - I, b - II, c - III, d - IV
a - IV, b - III, c - I, d - II
a - III, b - IV, c - I, d - II
a - IV, b - II, c - III, d - I
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). Sarcomere is the contractile unit of skeletal muscle; rigor mortis is extreme rigidity of muscles after death; iris muscles are ectodermal in origin; intercalated discs occur in cardiac muscle.

question: Which of following does not occur during contraction of muscle fibre?
options: Pulling of actin filaments towards middle of H zone
Binding of Ca2+ with calsequestrin protein
Reduction in length of I band
Chemical energy is converted into mechanical energy
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). Calsequestrin stores Ca2+ inside the sarcoplasmic reticulum. During contraction Ca2+ is released and binds troponin, not calsequestrin.

question: A motor unit is formed by (i) Single motor neuron (ii) Muscle fibres it innervates (iii) Neuromuscular junction
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). A motor unit is a single motor neuron together with the muscle fibres it innervates.

question: Mark the incorrect statement for myosin (thick) filament.
options: Each myosin filament is a polymerised protein
Its globular head has an active ATPase activity
It has binding sites for ATP as well as actin
The head is made up of LMM and form cross bridges with actin
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). The head and short arm of myosin are made of heavy meromyosin (HMM); light meromyosin (LMM) forms the tail. So (4) is incorrect.

question: Which of the following is incorrect w.r.t. muscle contraction? A. An increase in Ca++ in sarcoplasm leads to muscle contraction. B. Ca++ released from SR binds with tropomyosin. C. Acetylcholine esterase release in synapse increases muscle contraction. D. Muscle fibre remains relaxed till Ca++ in sarcoplasm is increased.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). B is incorrect (Ca2+ binds troponin). C is incorrect (acetylcholinesterase breaks down ACh and ends the signal). A and D are correct.

question: Cori's cycle operates between
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). In Cori's cycle, lactic acid from skeletal (voluntary) muscle is converted to glucose in the liver and returned to muscle.

question: Proteins which combine with Ca++ in voluntary and involuntary muscles are respectively
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). Striated (voluntary) muscle uses troponin; smooth (involuntary) muscle uses calmodulin.

question: Which of the following is not true with respect to white muscle fibres?
options: They contract for short periods of time
They have faster rate of contraction
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). White fibres have fewer mitochondria, contract fast for short periods, and have more (not less) sarcoplasmic reticulum. So (3) is not true.

question: The collagenous connective tissue sheath called "A" holds the numerous "B" which make up a skeletal muscle.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). A skeletal muscle is made of bundles of fibres (fascicles) held together by a collagenous connective tissue layer called fascia.

question: Arrange the following steps in correct sequence for skeletal muscle contraction A. [Ca+2] gradually increases in sarcoplasm. B. Calcium binds to troponin C. Troponin-tropomyosin move away from myosin binding sites on actin filaments. D. Neural signal at neuromuscular junction releases Acetylcholine. E. Action potential along sarcolemma. F. Actin-myosin cross- bridges formed D → E → B → A → C → F
options: D → E → A → B → C → F
D → B → E → C → A → F
D → B → A → C → E → F
(A) → Ca2+ binds troponin (B) → troponin-tropomyosin moves away (C) → crossbridges form (F).
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). ACh release (D) → action potential along sarcolemma (E) → Ca2+ rises in sarcoplasm

question: All the statements regarding muscle fibres are correct except one. Select the wrong statement
options: Tropomyosin is formed by the polymerisation of globular protein and is wrapped around the F-actin
During relaxation of muscle, the troponin component masks the active sites for the myosin head
The duration of twitch can vary in different muscles fibres
The globular head is an active Mg2+ dependent ATPase enzyme
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). F-actin is the polymer of globular G-actin; tropomyosin is a filamentous protein running along the F-actin, not a polymer of a globular protein. So (1) is wrong.

question: Arrange the events during muscle contraction in correct order. a. Acto-myosin complex synthesis. b. Release of neurotransmitter (acetylcholine) at the neuromuscular junction. c. Pumping of Ca2+ into sarcoplasmic cisternae. d. Sliding of actin filaments over myosin. e. Release of Ca2+ into sarcoplasm.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). Sequence: b (ACh release) → e (Ca2+ release) → a (cross-bridge/acto-myosin formation) → d (sliding) → c (Ca2+ pumped back).

question: Which statement is incorrect w.r.t. muscle contraction?
options: Sarcoplasmic membrane contains active transport pump for Ca+2
Ca2+ released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum combines with tropomyosin
Increase in Ca2+ concentration in the sarcoplasm causes increased contraction
Muscle action potential travels along the sarcolemma
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). Released Ca2+ binds to troponin (not tropomyosin).

question: Which of the following statement is incorrect w.r.t. skeletal muscle?
options: Two sarcomere are separated from each other by Krause line (Z-line)
I-band appears dark under the light microscope
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). The I-band (isotropic) appears light; the A-band appears dark.

question: Which of the following statement is incorrect?
options: Accumulation of lactic acid in muscle leads to pain.
Fresh ATP molecule is required for muscle relaxation.
Tetany is hyperexcitability of muscles which results in cramps and convulsions.
As the nerve impulse reaches the skeletal muscle fibre, the sarcolemma becomes impermeable to Na+.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). On arrival of the impulse, the sarcolemma becomes more permeable to Na+ (depolarisation), not impermeable.

question: Which of the following is incorrect w.r.t. comparison of red muscle fibres with white muscle fibres?
options: The former ones are thin and dark red is appearance.
The former ones rich in mitochondria and sarcoplasmic reticulum.
The former ones have slow rate of contraction.
The former ones can contract for a longer period without fatigue.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). Red fibres are rich in mitochondria but have less sarcoplasmic reticulum than white fibres, so (2) is incorrect.

question: Which of the following is major inorganic component of muscle?
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). As per the answer key, calcium is the major inorganic component.

question: Which of the following is not a character of white muscle fibres when compared to red muscle fibres?
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). White fibres are thicker, with fewer capillaries and mitochondria but more sarcoplasmic reticulum, so "less SR" is not their character.

question: Amongst the following, choose the process which can be classified as a muscle twitch
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). A hiccup is a single spasmodic contraction (twitch) of the diaphragm.

question: In which case amongst the following will rigor mortis appear earlier?
options: Polar bear which died of starvation in Arctic ice
A man who died a silent death after a prolonged illness
All of them will show similar time period
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). Rigor mortis appears earlier when ATP stores are depleted by strenuous activity, as in the soldier; cold slows its onset.

question: The interchange between muscle and liver lactic acid and glycogen is studied under the name of
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). This is Cori's cycle.

question: All the muscles have the following special properties, except
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). Autorhythmicity is shown only by some muscles (cardiac, some smooth); all muscles show excitability, extensibility, elasticity and contractility.

question: Which of the following features will not be true w.r.t. hypertrophy of muscles?
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). In hypertrophy the muscle fibres enlarge, but their number does not increase.

question: Which of the following do not occur at the time of contraction of striped muscle?
options: Binding of Ca++ with Troponin C
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). The filaments themselves do not shorten; they slide past each other.

question: Which of the following is not correct w.r.t. striated muscle fibres?
options: A-band consists of myosin filaments and parts of actin filaments
Each myosin filament is surrounded by 6 actin filaments
The calcium binding protein is calmodulin
T-tubules are present at the junction of A-I bands and are invagination of sarcolemma
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). In striated muscle the Ca2+ binding protein is troponin; calmodulin occurs in smooth muscle.

question: Select the correct sequence of events involved in contraction of striated muscles a. An action potential passes from the motor end plate finally reaching the SR and stimulate release of Ca2+ ions b. Binding of energized cross-bridges to myosin binding sites on actins c. Binding of Ca2+ with TpC-unit of troponin d. Movement of troponin-tropomyosin complex away from the myosin binding sites on actin e. Movement of the energized cross-bridges (power stroke) causing thin filaments to slide along the thick filaments
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). Sequence: a → c → d → b → e.

question: Choose the odd one w.r.t. smooth muscle fibres.
options: Calmodulin is the calcium binding protein
T-tubules are present close to Z-line
Iris and ciliary body muscles are multi-unit muscles
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). Smooth muscle fibres lack Z-lines and T-tubules, so (3) does not fit.

question: Globular protein which blocks active sites on F-actin when the muscle fibre is relaxed is
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). subunit of troponin masks the active sites; tropomyosin is filamentous.

question: When a stimulus several times greater than threshold stimulus is provided to a muscle fibre, the muscle fibre will
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). A muscle fibre obeys the all-or-none law: it contracts with the same force once threshold is reached.

question: Active transport of Ca2+ ions into the sarcoplasmic reticulum will not be associated with
options: Return of Z-lines to their original position
Increase in the I-band of sarcomere
Decrease in width of overlapping zone of a sarcomere
Decrease in the width of H-zone of a sarcomere
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). Pumping Ca2+ back means relaxation: Z-lines return, I-band and H-zone widen and overlap decreases. A decrease in H-zone width occurs in contraction, so it is not associated.

question: Choose the incorrect statement
options: Ca2+ play key regulatory role in muscle contraction
The last two pairs of ribs do not participate in breathing
Carpometacarpal joint of thumb is an example of saddle joint
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). Tropomyosin is a filamentous (fibrous) protein wrapped around F-actin.

question: During hypertrophy of the muscles which of the following will not increase?
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). In hypertrophy fibre size increases but fibre number does not.

question: Each myosin is surrounded by ________ actin filaments on either side. Choose the option that correctly fills the blank.

question: At the time of skeletal muscle contraction, which of the following will not occur?

question: Select the feature which is not associated with white muscle fibres

They depend mainly on glycolysis for energy production and soon get fatigued
Less sarcoplasmic reticulum compared to red muscle fibres
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). White fibres have more sarcoplasmic reticulum than red fibres.

question: Autorhythmicity is exhibited by both
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle

question: Choose the incorrect statement with respect to myosin.
options: Globular head part has actin binding site
Has light meromyosin and heavy meromyosin
Tropomyosin run close to the meromyosin throughout its length
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). Tropomyosin runs along the F-actin filament, not along myosin.

question: Extra amount of oxygen consumed during recovery from muscle fatigue is called oxygen debt of the muscle. It is used in oxidizing what percentage of accumulated lactic acid aerobically and in restoring the depleted creatine phosphate and ATP in muscle fibre?
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). About 20% of the accumulated lactic acid is oxidised aerobically; the rest (about 80%) is reconverted to glycogen.

question: During muscle contraction, the following events occur a. Release of Ca++ from sarcoplasmic reticulum b. Ca++ expose actins which bind to the myosin heads to form cross bridges c. A motor neuron carries signal to the muscle fibre which generates an action potential in it d. Cross bridges are broken and muscle relaxes e. These cross bridges pull the actin filaments, causing them to slide over the myosin filaments and thereby causing contraction. Select the correct sequence.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). Motor signal (c) → Ca2+ release (a) → cross-bridge formation (b) → sliding (e) → relaxation (d).

question: Which of the following properties is not applicable to the myosin filaments?

Cross arms present, hence have rough surface
Found only in the A-band of sarcomere

ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). It is the actin (thin) filaments that slide toward/into the H-zone; myosin filaments stay in the A-band.

ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (4). Sequence: b → a → c → e → d.

question: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: Sternum is present on ventral side of human body
In a muscle fibre, Ca++ is stored in sarcoplasmic reticulum
Tropomyosin is present in thick filaments
H-zone of skeletal muscle fibre represents only thick filaments

question: The contractile and regulatory proteins of a muscle are respectively

question: During muscle contraction, which of the following is incorrect?

solution: Correct option is (3). The sarcomere shortens during contraction.

question: The thin filaments are firmly attached with Z-line and are surrounded by myosin filaments. Which membrane bisects I-band in the centre?

ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). The Z-line lies at the centre of the I-band.

question: Following are some events occurring during muscle contraction. Arrange them in a sequence a. Action potential of muscle fibre occurs. b. Sarcoplasmic reticulum releases stored Ca+2 that binds with troponin component of thin filament. c. Neurotransmitter released at neuromuscular junction. d. Ca+2 is pumped back into SR and troponin masks the active site. e. Actin molecules are exposed and cross bridges are formed. Choose the correct option.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). Neurotransmitter release (c) → action potential (a) → Ca2+ release and binding (b) → cross-bridges (e) → relaxation (d).

question: All of the given statements are correct w.r.t. the mechanism of muscle contraction except one. Choose the incorrect statement.
options: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system via sensory neuron
Action potential for contraction spreads through the muscle fibre and causes the release of calcium ions into the sarcoplasm
Increase in calcium ions level leads to the binding of calcium with a subunit of troponin on actin filaments and thereby remove the masking of active sites of myosin
Utilising the energy from ATP hydrolysis, the myosin head now binds to the exposed active sites on actin to form a crossbridge
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). The signal reaches muscle through a motor neuron, not a sensory neuron.

question: The contractile protein of skeletal muscle possessing Mg2+ dependent ATPase activity is
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). The globular head of myosin has Mg2+-dependent ATPase activity.

question: Which of the following muscle tissues has longest refractory period and can use lactic acid produced by skeletal muscle fibres to make ATP?
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). Cardiac muscle has a long refractory period (prevents tetany) and can use lactic acid as fuel.

question: Read the following statements very carefully A. Muscle fibres carry out considerable aerobic oxidation. B. Muscle fibres have slow rate of contraction. C. hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). A and B are true for red fibres; C (less mitochondria) and D (lighter, thicker) describe white fibres. Two are correct.

question: In resting state, a subunit of ______ masks the active binding sites for myosin on actin filaments. Choose the option that correctly fills the blank.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). Troponin (via tropomyosin) masks the myosin-binding sites on actin at rest.

question: Each organised skeletal muscle in our body is made of a number of A held together by a common collagenous connective tissue layer called B. Choose the option which correctly fills the blanks labelled as A and B
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). Muscle is made of fascicles (muscle bundles) held together by fascia.

question: Which statement is correct for muscle contraction?
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (b). H-line becomes narrow during contraction while I-band shortens during contraction and Z- line is not affected by contraction. The A-band (thick filaments) retains its length.

question: What is sarcomere?
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (d). Dark bands on the myofibril form the A-band. The middle part of the A-band contains light zones - Hensen line (H-lines). Light band on the myofibril is called I-band. The middle part of the I- band contains Z-lines. Sarcomere is the part between two Z-lines.

question: Which of the following is the most abundant protein in a muscle?
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (a). Myosin: The thick filament protein responsible for muscle contraction. It forms the largest fraction(35% to 50%) of muscle protein.

question: The functional unit of contractile system in striated muscle is
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (b). Myofibril is the filament comprising the muscle fibre. Z band marks the two ends of the sarcomere. Cross bridges are present on the myosin head.

question: Which ion is essential for muscle contraction?
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (c). Movement of Ca2+ out of the sarcoplasmic reticulum controls the making and breaking of the actin-myosin complex. Actomyosin is the complex due to which muscle contraction and relaxation take place.

question: Intercostal muscles occur in
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (c). Intercostal muscles (external intercostals and internal intercostals) are attached with the ribs and help in the movement of the rib cage during breathing.

question: Statement I: Skeletal muscles are striated and voluntary. Statement II: Cardiac muscles are striated and voluntary.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). Statement I is correct: skeletal muscles have a striped appearance and are under voluntary control of the nervous system. Statement II is incorrect: cardiac muscles are striated but involuntary, as the nervous system does not control their activity directly.

question: Read the following statements about types of muscles. I. Visceral muscles are smooth and involuntary. II. Cardiac muscles are branched, striated and involuntary. III. Skeletal muscles are primarily involved in locomotory actions and changes of body postures. IV. Skeletal muscles are non-striated. Choose the correct option.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). I, II and III are correct. IV is incorrect: skeletal muscles have a striped appearance and hence are called striated muscles.

question: Read the following statements. I. Muscle is a specialised tissue of mesodermal origin. II. About 40-50 per cent of the body weight of a human adult is contributed by muscles. III. Visceral muscles are located in the wall of the heart. IV. The nervous system directly controls the activity of cardiac muscle. Choose the correct option.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). I and II are true. III is false: visceral (smooth) muscles are found in the inner walls of hollow visceral organs such as the alimentary canal and reproductive tract; cardiac muscles are the muscles of the heart. IV is false: cardiac muscles are involuntary because the nervous system does not control them directly.

question: Statement I: A muscle fibre is a syncitium as its sarcoplasm contains many nuclei. Statement II: Cardiac muscle cells assemble in a branching pattern; they are striated and involuntary.

Neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). Both statements are correct as given in the text on muscle structure and types.

question: Which of the following statements is incorrect? I. Muscle bundles (fascicles) are held together by a collagenous connective tissue layer called fascia. II. A muscle fibre is a syncitium because its sarcoplasm contains many nuclei. III. The sarcolemma is the endoplasmic reticulum of the muscle fibre. IV. The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the storehouse of calcium ions.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). I, II and IV are correct. III is incorrect: the sarcolemma is the plasma membrane lining the muscle fibre and enclosing the sarcoplasm; the endoplasmic reticulum of the fibre is called the sarcoplasmic reticulum.

question: Statement I: The 'Z' line bisects the 'A' band. Statement II: The 'M' line holds the thick filaments together in the middle of the 'A' band.

Neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct

ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). Statement I is incorrect: the 'Z' line is an elastic fibre in the centre of each 'I' band and bisects it. Statement II is correct: the thick filaments of the 'A' band are held together in the middle by a thin fibrous membrane called the 'M' line.

question: Read the following statements about a myofibril. I. The 'Z' line bisects the 'I' band. II. The 'M' line lies in the middle of the 'A' band. III. Thin filaments are firmly attached to the 'M' line. IV. The portion between two successive 'Z' lines is a sarcomere. Choose the correct option.

ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). I, II and IV are correct. III is wrong: thin (actin) filaments are firmly attached to the 'Z' line, while the thick (myosin) filaments are held at the 'M' line.

question: Consider the following statements regarding a sarcomere. I. The 'H' zone is the central part of the thick filaments that is not overlapped by thin filaments. II. The 'H' zone widens during contraction. III. During contraction the 'I' band gets reduced whereas the 'A' band retains its length. Choose the correct option.
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). I and III are correct. II is incorrect: during contraction the thin filaments slide towards the centre of the 'A' band, so the region not overlapped by them (the 'H' zone) becomes narrower.

question: Statement I: During muscle contraction the 'Z' lines are pulled inwards, shortening the sarcomere. Statement II: During muscle contraction the length of the 'A' band decreases.

Neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). Statement I is correct: cross bridges pull the actin filaments (attached to the 'Z' lines) towards the centre of the 'A' band. Statement II is incorrect: the 'A' band (thick filaments) retains its length; only the 'I' band and 'H' zone are reduced.

question: During maximal contraction of a sarcomere, consider the following. I. The 'H' zone may disappear. II. The length of the 'A' band remains constant. III. The thin filaments shorten. Choose the correct option.

ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). I and II are correct (Fig. 17.5: the thin filaments meet in the centre and the 'H' zone vanishes while the 'A' band stays the same). III is incorrect: the thin filaments slide inwards; they do not shorten.

question: Read the following statements. I. An actin filament is made of two 'F' actins helically wound around each other. II. Each 'G' actin is a polymer of 'F' actins. III. Two filaments of tropomyosin run close to the 'F' actins throughout their length. IV. In the resting state a subunit of troponin unmasks the active binding sites for myosin. ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). I and III are correct. II is false: each 'F' (filamentous) actin is a polymer of monomeric 'G' (globular) actins. IV is false: at rest a subunit of troponin masks the active binding sites for myosin on actin. Hence two statements are correct.

question: Which of the following statements about myosin is incorrect? I. A meromyosin has two parts - heavy meromyosin (HMM) and light meromyosin (LMM). II. The head and short arm of HMM project outwards and are known as the cross arm. III. The globular head is an active ATPase with binding sites for ATP and active sites for actin. IV. solution: Correct option is (4). I, II and III are correct. IV is incorrect: the globular head with the short arm is the HMM, whereas the LMM is the tail of the meromyosin.

question: Statement I: The sarcoplasmic reticulum of a muscle fibre is the storehouse of calcium ions. Statement II: Ca++ binds to tropomyosin to remove the masking of the active sites on actin.

Neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct

ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect: the released Ca++ binds to a subunit of troponin on the actin filaments, which removes the masking of the active sites for myosin.

question: Statement I: The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma of a muscle fibre is called the neuromuscular junction (motor-end plate). Statement II: A neural signal reaching this junction releases acetylcholine, which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). Both statements are correct as described in the mechanism of muscle contraction: the neurotransmitter acetylcholine released at the motor-end plate generates an action potential in the sarcolemma.

question: Statement I: A motor unit consists of a motor neuron only. Statement II: The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma is called the motor-end plate.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). Statement I is incorrect: a motor unit is a motor neuron along with the muscle fibres connected to it. Statement II is correct: the neuromuscular junction is also called the motor-end plate.

question: Statement I: Cross-bridge formation between myosin and actin utilises energy from ATP hydrolysis. Statement II: Breaking of the cross bridge requires binding of a new ATP to the myosin head.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct
hint: Hint for Muscle: Focus on NCERT Locomotion and Movement - Muscle.
ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). Both are correct. The myosin head (ATPase) hydrolyses ATP and binds to the exposed active sites on actin; after the sliding, a new ATP binds and the cross bridge is broken.

question: Arrange the following events of muscle contraction in the correct sequence. ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (1). Neural signal releases acetylcholine (iv), which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma (ii); this causes release of Ca++ into the sarcoplasm (iii); Ca++ binds to troponin (i), unmasking the active sites, and cross bridges form (v).

question: Read the following statements about muscle contraction. I. Binding of Ca++ to a subunit of troponin precedes cross-bridge formation. II. Breaking of a cross bridge requires binding of a fresh ATP. III. After releasing ADP and Pi, the myosin head returns to its relaxed state. IV. question: Read the following statements about relaxation of muscle. I. Ca++ ions are pumped back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae, resulting in masking of actin filaments. II. The 'Z' lines return

ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (2). I, II and III are correct. IV is incorrect: release of Ca++ into the sarcoplasm leads to contraction; relaxation follows when Ca++ is pumped back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae.

question: Read the following statements about the sliding filament theory. I. Contraction of a muscle fibre takes place by sliding of thin filaments over thick filaments. II. The thick filaments shorten during contraction. III. The sarcomere shortens during contraction. Choose the correct option.

ncertRef: NCERT Class XI • Locomotion and Movement • Muscle
solution: Correct option is (3). I and III are correct. II is incorrect: the filaments do not shorten; the thin filaments slide over the thick filaments, pulling the 'Z' lines inwards so that the sarcomere shortens.

question: Read the following statements. I. Repeated activation of muscles causes accumulation of lactic acid due to anaerobic breakdown of glycogen, causing fatigue. II. question: Statement I: Red muscle fibres can also be called aerobic muscles. Statement II: White muscle fibres have a high amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum.
